defects.observation: The exact 512px export shows an alternating stack of short slash-like grooves, but the shorter nested subdivisions do not resolve as coherent subordinate branches within broad primary units. Hero and clay nearly flatten the feature. The additional real neutral-gray top render confirms that this is not merely a color choice.
defects.obligation: Original frozen brief recognition_features[1] and concept_decisions require tightly packed alternating primary units with nested subordinate relief, intended at256–512px; Dunn2019 Fig1F and morphology discussion support a branching hierarchy, not a living fern.
defects.geometry_diagnosis: The current generator samples a whole slab on44 lateral by132 longitudinal cells. Only a fraction of those lateral samples fall inside the frond, while secondary relief oscillates about6.2 times across each half width. At broad lower rows the half frond has roughly8–10 lateral sample intervals, falling further toward the tip. This supports undersampling/aliasing as a cause, not absence of procedural intent.
defects.required_correction: Create a new isolated revision. Reallocate topology from blank slab into the frond or use explicit branch-aligned local topology. Preserve continuous broad alternating primary units and make a smaller simplified set of short nested subbranch ridges/grooves that read as subdivisions within them. Keep the original shallow integral fossil impression, slight axial bend, no invented stalk/holdfast/living underside, original nominal scale and BGS GSM105873 non-holotype scope. Do not substitute lighting, camera, material contrast or scope relabeling for geometry.
defects.retest: Inspect a small genuine diagnostic top/neutral-gray top and hero at256–512px before full lifecycle. If geometry resolves the original recognition criterion, bind the new exact GLB/brief/references, rerun affected source/export, two genuine semantic rebuilds, validation/runtime parse and all eight final views, followed by targeted independent difference/regression review.
